rows.note: Brake noise/shake progressing to total failure, no subtype detail -- the standard brake schema conflict.
Backup camera showing a black screen in reverse is a backup-camera failure, not a lighting failure. Gold is wrong.
Generic rant ('consumers are being ripped off... no safety defect') names no system at all. Gold is wrong.

Two named issues: stalling with no diagnosed cause ('beyond the ability of service technicians to diagnose') and explicitly worsening 'electrical malfunctions.' No engine-specific cause is ever named, so plain ENGINE doesn't fit; UNKNOWN OR OTHER fits the undiagnosed stall, ELECTRICAL SYSTEM fits the named malfunctions. Gold's ENGINE is the weakest of the three readings.
Frame rust/flaking, body otherwise fine, no suspension component named. Teacher is right, gold is wrong.
Narrative explicitly says 'GAS' -- the more specific gasoline-tied class fits better than the generic fallback. Teacher is right.
Ticking sound, engine failure -- no coolant/overheating symptom anywhere in the text. Teacher is right, gold overreached.
Hood flew open while driving -- our own definition names 'hood latches' explicitly. Teacher is right, gold is wrong.

'Death wobble' where the dealer replaced the steering dampener specifically -- same pattern as 1811665 (steering linkage damper), which pins it to STEERING rather than the generic wobble ambiguity. Gold is right, teacher is wrong.

No brake mention anywhere in the text -- gold is unsupported. Vehicle moved backwards then forwards uncontrollably; could be unintended acceleration (VEHICLE SPEED CONTROL) or an erratic transmission engagement fault (POWER TRAIN, teacher's answer) -- no diagnosis is given to prefer one.
'NO SUMMARY LISTED' -- zero content. Teacher is right, gold has no support.
Three unrelated symptoms (leaking push rod, squeaking brakes, turn signal cutoff) with no stated primary concern -- genuinely multi-issue.

'ENGINE FAILED' does name a specific system, so UNKNOWN OR OTHER doesn't fit; no coolant symptom, so plain ENGINE is the better single answer than gold's cooling-specific class. Both gold and teacher are wrong.
Literal wiper failure -- the established B12 VISIBILITY-vs-VISIBILITY/WIPER inconsistency, both accepted.

Unintended acceleration AND steering-wheel lockup are both explicitly named -- two real systems identified, so gold's UNKNOWN OR OTHER doesn't fit ('narrative doesn't identify any specific system' -- it identifies two).
The stated problem is jerking under braking; wheel bearings/wheels/tires were replaced as repair ATTEMPTS, not separate complaints. This is a brake complaint, not suspension -- gold is wrong.

Chronicle of multiple failures (gaskets, transmission, engine) culminating in a power-steering hose fire -- the most recent and most acute event described (with a fire) is the steering-fluid fire, but the transmission failure is also explicitly named. Genuinely multi-issue across time.

Moisture intrusion into a specific tail light causing it to malfunction/crack -- the lighting itself is the stated problem, matching our EXTERIOR LIGHTING definition precisely. Teacher is right, gold is too general.

Dealer's actual repair replaced the rim -- matches WHEELS ('wheel rim cracking/bending') directly; no strut/control-arm/ball-joint symptom is named to support SUSPENSION. Gold is right, teacher is wrong.

Diagnostic codes P2440/P2442 are secondary air injection -- an emissions/exhaust-system fault, which our confirmed convention (gotcha B16) routes to ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING, not fuel delivery and not plain ENGINE. Both gold and teacher are wrong.
No response from the accelerator, surging/lurching, wrench light -- textbook accelerator-pedal-response failure, no transmission/gear symptom named. Teacher is right, gold is wrong.

Complainant explicitly frames it as 'my engine failing while driving. Stalling...' as the primary, most-emphasized concern, later confirmed by a timing-chain repair (engine-internal). Heater/radio glitches are secondary. Teacher is right, gold is wrong.
Exhaust bolts breaking off -- per the confirmed exhaust-system convention (gotcha B16), this rolls to ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING. Gold is right, teacher is wrong.

Broad electrical cascade (shuts off, hard restart, horn/wipers/washer/lights activating randomly, erratic speedometer) with zero mention of stability/skid control. Teacher is right, gold has no textual support at all.

Complainant's own diagnosis names the root cause as the 'power control module,' a general electrical component, and the AC (not just the turn signals) is also affected. Teacher is right, gold only captures one symptom.
A malfunctioning passenger-seat occupancy sensor is literally part of the airbag deployment system. Teacher is right, gold has no textual support.

Garbled dealer explanation: an expanding 'gas can' (likely gas tank) damaged the frame. Root cause (fuel system) and stated consequence (frame damage, the reason it's a total loss) are both defensible.
Brake-pedal-ineffective-plus-unintended-acceleration is the same B5 human-judgment-ceiling pattern already accepted both ways for 1056493.
Ignition/starting malfunction (root cause, ELECTRICAL) leads directly to an RPM/speed surge that doesn't respond to braking (symptom, VEHICLE SPEED CONTROL) -- both explicitly named.

Spark-plug-family complaint; matches the already-confirmed majority convention for this exact pattern (gotcha, cmplid 17193: ENGINE outnumbers ELECTRICAL SYSTEM ~2.2:1 for spark-plug narratives). Teacher is right.
Explicitly diagnosed faulty gasoline fuel pump with burnt wiring -- the specific class fits better than the generic fallback. Teacher is right.

The actual physical symptom described is 'steering locked up, difficult to turn' -- gold only picked up on one of three dashboard warning lights mentioned, not the described symptom. Teacher is right.

Master tech confirmed a snapped timing chain causing catastrophic engine failure; the power-steering warning was a downstream consequence of the engine shutting off, not an independent steering defect. Teacher is right, gold is wrong.

Neither original answer is right. The gear-disengagement failure is explicitly tied to the hybrid battery dropping under 3% charge, and the narrative cites the i3's known battery-related defect -- this is the rare HYBRID PROPULSION SYSTEM category by definition, not general POWER TRAIN or VEHICLE SPEED CONTROL.
Undiagnosed knocking noise from the rear wheel area, dealer denies any issue -- no part is named to prefer one system over the other.
Narrative explicitly names 'transmission issue' as the root cause; nothing about wiring/battery/fuses is mentioned. Teacher is right, gold has no textual support.
Misfire on 4 of 6 cylinders from wrong factory spark plugs, no coolant/overheating symptom at all. Teacher is right, gold overreached.

'All power will turn off' with no named component (no wiring/battery/fuse/ignition mentioned) -- fits our own UNKNOWN OR OTHER definition exactly. Gold is right, teacher overreached to ELECTRICAL SYSTEM without a named part.
Explicitly named: 'EPB (Electronic Parking Brake) Issue.' Teacher is right, gold's generic fallback ignores the named subtype.

Both named failures (rear power window motor, rear climate system not blowing heat with no defrost mention) are specific OEM-accessory-style component failures, not a case of 'no system identified.' Teacher is right.
